capabilities: Assign letter keys to custom highlight colours in settings
Apply coloured highlights inline with ==x key syntax while typing
extras: The README shows default key-colour assignments only as a code example; no screenshots or configuration walkthrough beyond the ==x format, and the ==x trigger must be followed by a space.
intentEvidence: QuickColour allows you to assign a letter key to the end of the default Obsidian highlight key ==
motivation: The author loves writing with colour but never wants to touch the mouse, so existing mouse-driven highlight plugins did not fit their workflow.
problem: Existing highlight colour plugins require selecting text with the mouse and picking a colour from a menu, which breaks keyboard-only writing.

relations.evidence: Existing highlight colour plugins require dragging your mouse over text and selecting colour from a menu.

summary: Highlighting plugin that lets you assign letter keys to custom highlight colours, applied inline with ==x syntax while typing.
